context.title: Sample debate — AI regulation and energy policy
context.description: A two-person policy debate on AI regulation and the energy cost of compute. Dr. Lena Farrow argues the regulatory framework is already settled; Marc Devereux argues the binding constraint is energy and capital, not law.

segments.speaker: Dr. Lena Farrow
segments.text: Let's be honest about where regulation actually stands today.

segments.speaker: Dr. Lena Farrow
segments.text: The EU AI Act entered into force in August 2024, so this is settled law, not a proposal.

segments.speaker: Dr. Lena Farrow
segments.text: And it bans facial recognition outright across the entire European Union.

segments.speaker: Marc Devereux
segments.text: That second part is where I think you're overstating the case considerably.

segments.speaker: Marc Devereux
segments.text: But set that aside. My concern is energy, because these systems are not free to run.

segments.speaker: Marc Devereux
segments.text: Data centres consumed roughly 1.5 percent of global electricity in 2024, and that share is climbing fast.

segments.speaker: Dr. Lena Farrow
segments.text: Climbing from a small base. And the grid is getting cleaner at the same time.

segments.speaker: Dr. Lena Farrow
segments.text: The International Energy Agency said back in 2020 that solar is now the cheapest electricity in history.

segments.speaker: Marc Devereux
segments.text: Cheapest to build, maybe. That is not the same thing as cheapest to deliver at three in the morning.

segments.speaker: Marc Devereux
segments.text: France generates more than seventy percent of its electricity from nuclear power, and that is what firm capacity looks like.

segments.speaker: Dr. Lena Farrow
segments.text: Nobody disputes his French number. I dispute what he concludes from it.

segments.speaker: Marc Devereux
segments.text: Then let's talk cost. Training a single frontier model now costs over a billion dollars a run.

segments.speaker: Marc Devereux
segments.text: That is a barrier to entry that no amount of open weights is going to fix.

segments.speaker: Dr. Lena Farrow
segments.text: That billion dollar figure is doing an enormous amount of work in his argument.

segments.speaker: Dr. Lena Farrow
segments.text: Meanwhile small open models run on a laptop, which is rather the point of this whole conversation.

segments.speaker: Marc Devereux
segments.text: On a laptop, badly. And she knows the quality gap is real.
